name: traceroost
description: Agentic AI monitoring and observability — OTEL traces and local log file ingestion for Copilot, Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, and Cursor CLI. VS Code extension, npx, and Docker.
author: TraceRoost

commands.title: TraceRoost: Link This Machine to an Org (Cloud)

walkthroughs.title: Get Started with TraceRoost
walkthroughs.description: Observe and debug your AI agent traces in real time.

steps.title: What is TraceRoost?
steps.description:
TraceRoost gives you a live observability dashboard for GitHub Copilot, Claude Code, and Codex (plus OpenCode and Cursor CLI from their local logs) — token usage, latency, file changes, and loop detection.

[Open TraceRoost Sidebar](command:workbench.view.extension.traceroost)

steps.title: Agents Are Ready
steps.description: Unless auto-configuration is turned off (traceRoost.autoConfigureAgents), TraceRoost configured your agents to send telemetry to the local collector. Restart any running agents to start collecting traces. Past trace history is already loading from local log files — no restart needed to see it.

steps.title: Start an Agent Run
steps.description: Run Copilot, Claude Code, or Codex and the dashboard will populate in real time.

steps.title: Open the Full Dashboard
steps.description:
The sidebar shows a live summary. Open the full dashboard in an editor panel for traces, diffs, alerts, cost estimation, export, and more.

[Open Dashboard](command:traceRoost.openDashboard)

steps.title: Detect Loops and Inefficiencies
steps.description: The Traces tab flags seventeen stuck-agent and waste signals per trace — tool-call deadlocks, error spirals, context accumulation, avoidable cache misses, and more. The Advisor tab analyzes patterns across traces to generate specific suggestions for improving your agent instruction file.

traceRoost.otlpPort.description: Local port for OTLP trace receiver

traceRoost.autoConfigureAgents.description: Automatically write OTEL telemetry settings into Claude Code's (~/.claude/settings.json), Codex's (~/.codex/config.toml), and GitHub Copilot's own configuration so they send trace data to TraceRoost. Runs on every activation but only rewrites a file when something's actually missing, so it's silent after the first successful run (shows a notification only when it changes something). Disabling this leaves your agents' configuration untouched — you can still trigger it manually with the Configure OTEL button in Settings, configure OTEL by hand (see the Help tab's Setup section), or rely on traceRoost.enableLogIngestion alone. Codex and Copilot CLI traces have little to show without OTEL: their log files carry only aggregate totals, no per-turn tool calls or responses.

traceRoost.enableOtelIngestion.description: Accept incoming OTEL span data. The OTLP server keeps listening on traceRoost.otlpPort regardless; disabling this silently drops received payloads without storing them.

traceRoost.enableLogIngestion.description: Read the local logs and databases Claude Code, Codex, Copilot CLI, Copilot Chat, OpenCode, and Cursor CLI write as a data source. Log data has lower fidelity than OTEL — timing, speed, and loop signals are not available for Codex and Copilot CLI, whose log files carry only aggregate totals. When OTEL captured the same trace (always detected for Claude Code), the OTEL entry wins and the log entry is dropped; otherwise the two can appear as separate entries. Loading is done incrementally in the background and will not block the UI.

traceRoost.enableMcpServer.description: Start the TraceRoost MCP server so Claude Code can query your trace history. The server listens on traceRoost.mcpPort (default 4316). See the TraceRoost Help tab → MCP for setup instructions.

traceRoost.mcpPort.description: Local port for the TraceRoost MCP server (when traceRoost.enableMcpServer is true). Register it with Claude Code with: claude mcp add --transport http --scope user traceroost http://localhost:4316/mcp

traceRoost.sessionRetentionDays.description: How many days to keep trace history in the local database. Older traces (and their blob files) are deleted automatically on activation and every 24 hours.

scripts.compile: pnpm run check-types && pnpm run lint && node esbuild.js
scripts.fixtures:check: node demo/generate-fixtures.js --dir /tmp/traceroost-fixtures && pnpm run compile-tests && node demo/validate-fixtures.js --dir /tmp/traceroost-fixtures
scripts.package: pnpm run check-types && pnpm run lint && node esbuild.js --production
scripts.package:core: pnpm run check-types && pnpm run lint && node esbuild.js --production --edition=core && node scripts/check-edition.mjs core
scripts.pretest: pnpm run compile-tests && pnpm run compile && pnpm run lint
scripts.clean-tests: node -e "for (const d of ['out/test', 'out/test-media', 'out/test-standalone']) require('fs').rmSync(d, { recursive: true, force: true })"
scripts.test:unit: pnpm run clean-tests && pnpm run compile-tests && pnpm run compile-tests:media && pnpm run compile-tests:standalone && mocha
scripts.test:coverage: pnpm run clean-tests && pnpm run compile-tests && pnpm run compile-tests:media && pnpm run compile-tests:standalone && c8 mocha --reporter dot
